reviews.text: The Killer might not be among David Fincher’s best works but it does stand out for its performances and technical excellence.
reviews.author: Ganesh Aaglave

reviews.text: The Killer possesses many of Fincher’s traits but falls short of being truly satisfying. Whether that is the intention or not, the detachment and indifference which goes hand in glove with this assassin, robs The Killer of something essential.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: A slick, tongue-in-cheek take on the hitman movie.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: “The Killer” is a slickly crafted beast that leaves you clutching your seat as its psychotic protagonist follows his mission through to its predictably bloody conclusion.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: The Killer is not a good film, it is misguided from beginning to end. Why should anyone care about the central character or most of the others?
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: It's pure Fincher on all fronts, and that's reason to rejoice.
reviews.author: Paul Klein

reviews.text: The Killer is David Fincher playing to his cold and precise strengths, to a mostly positive execution.
reviews.author: Shakyl Lambert

reviews.text: This is the worst dressed, most haggard cinematic assassin in recent memory, with the ugliest beach villa.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: The Killer does provide a fine showcase for some expert close-up fight choreography, but the same attention to detail doesn't extend to the film's contrived, confusing plot and lazy stock characters.
reviews.author: Jamie Healy

reviews.text: It plays like a John Wick flick for people who think they’re too good for a John Wick flick.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The Killer evaporates before your eyes, undone by an obtrusive voiceover narration that undermines its sleek minimalism at nearly every turn.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Just like only David Fincher knows how to do it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: A stark and stylish hit man drama that makes maximum use of the magnetism of Michael Fassbender.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Even the fact that the film itself is a technical marvel, sleek perfection from start to finish, is part of the gag.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: The Killer is a self-referential work in which Fincher acknowledges his own reputation as a controlling director and digs under the surface to find the quivering child beneath. He’s there, but you have to look for him.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: The Killer feels like the Rosetta Stone for David Fincher: the core of his entire thesis as an artist.
reviews.author: Mitchell Beaupre

reviews.text: A satisfying film, yet I can't tell whether Fincher appreciates that his variations on the formula are still formula.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: An uneven revenge thriller without the emotional depth to match its visual prowess. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: In "The Killer,” a superb Fassbender is at the heart of almost every frame of the film. You could call it a Shakespearean performance. His acting in the thought-provoking, existential movie is a tour-de-force.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Death, “The Killer” seems to say, is just another commodity — like office space at WeWork or a McDonald’s hamburger — and Fincher depicts Fassbender’s assassin as the Grim Reaper as the ultimate vulture capitalist.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Michael Fassbender, another artist who should also have two Oscars, gives a restrained yet potent portrait of a man who must suddenly protect what he loves. Add a stunning turn by Tilda Swinton...
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: David Fincher strips away the assassination thriller to its essentials ...
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: Fassbender kills it as The Killer.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: The director finds the center of all his obsessions in a new exploration of the killer from his context, taking elements from "Seven" and "Zodiac" [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: Rather than being a high-energy action film, this is more of a movie about a particular occupation and a particular worldview. It also explores human nature a bit around the edges.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The protagonist’s professional philosophy sums up my feelings toward this solidly-crafted but emotionally reticent film: “It comes down to preparation, attention to details, redundancies, redundancies and redundancies.”
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: It has a massive, house-leveling fight scene, but dramatically it doesn’t really develop a pulse until its final minutes.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: This film is a good demonstration that not everything between comic panels is worth showing.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: This is probably the closest David Fincher will ever get to making one of those Fabelman-esque autobiographies, as he picks at the brilliant procedure that’s marked his filmography.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: The Killer works because there’s more than mere automaton stylings. There’s a tension, heightened by each tight frame and scrupulous composition...
reviews.author: Beatrice Loayza

reviews.text: For those of us who love Fincher's obsessive characters, dry humor and icy detachment, it's right on target.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: I knew all the details when I saw him remove the bread from an Egg McMuffin, or how he takes an extra second to appreciate himself in the mirror while on the move. Fassbender is a force to reckon with, and he never even raises his voice.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: This portrait of a meticulous murderer-for-hire is well-crafted and consuming, at least until a climactic scene that, at least upon first viewing, rings a bit false.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: The devil's in the details, and David Fincher is a master of details.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: It’s thrilling, high-level filmmaking.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: David Fincher’s new movie The Killer is supposedly a metacommentary on hit-man films — and possibly on the director himself. Or that could just be an excuse for how boring it is.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: [David Fincher] certainly has powerhouse craft when all cylinders are firing -- which they are in this movie... A first-rate neo-noir.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: [It has] the best fight scene I've seen in a movie in a long, long time. It's thrilling. I really, really dug this.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: Just as the film seems to be setting up the same-old, same-old tropes, Fincher signals he might be delivering a slow, sneaky deconstruction of the hitman mystique.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Ultimately, The Killer is just a fun, pulpy romp that is more akin to the plug-and-play adventures of I.O. Interactive’s Hitman series than a profound statement on the culture at large.
reviews.author: Peter Bell

reviews.text: The Killer’s disguise as a trash genre exercise has elicited plenty of shrugs, but make no mistake, it’s every bit as potent and layered as Fincher’s masterworks of The Social Network and Fight Club.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: If ever a film embodied the spirit of its director, The Killer would definitely be that film.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: While some may expect more from this dark revenge thriller, the result doesn't disappoint.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The Killer might suggest Fincher is grappling with his label as a cold, clinical genius, who prioritises perfection over vulnerability, precision over humanity... Deep down somewhere, despite what he has said in the past, David Fincher still gives a fuck.
reviews.author: Tatsam Mukherjee

reviews.text: Cold bloodied and terrifying, but it sure does hold your attention.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: What does it take to be a paid assassin? Director David Fincher (‘Fight Club,” “Zodiac,” “The Social Network”) explores the qualifications in the cerebral neo-noir.
reviews.author: Tim Miller

reviews.text: The Killer won’t be remembered alongside David Fincher’s best, but that speaks more to the quality of his past work than the failings of this film.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: A perfectly pitched crime thriller that's David Fincher's best film in a decade
reviews.author: Savina Petkova

reviews.text: While the film is enjoyable to watch it just doesn't bring anything new to genre - and that is something I have always expected from David Fincher in the past.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: Think of this film as a corporate JOHN WICK. It's about revenge and it exists solely in the headspace and environments of the lead character's ilk. Civilians become window-dressing as Fassbender narrates the monotony and mantras that keep him alive.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It may be a far cry from Fincher heavyweights like Se7en, Fight Club and Gone Girl), but considering how bleak and serious so many of his movies are, the pulpy feel of The Killer makes it a welcome addition to his catalogue.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: The Killer is an opportunity for America’s most stylish director to reboot, to get back to basics, to come in under two hours.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: The Killer is a film about a man who is bad at his job, how long you find that premise intriguing will correlate directly to how much you enjoy it.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: In its event horizon, it is a sophisticated, tense and entertaining thriller from Fincher. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Fincher’s rejection of The Smiths aims to destroy the band’s great contributions to civilization. This anti-art horror film appeals to the hipster appetite for self-destruction.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: David Fincher strikes a delicious balance with this neo-noir thriller about a methodical hitman: it is one of his slightest but most enjoyable feature films.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: In the end, I was somewhat amused and impressed with “The Killer’s” execution but found the story lacking, the protagonist, muddied. I couldn’t help but feel that I had consumed a meal of empty calories, leaving me hungry for more substance.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Amidst the deliberate storytelling, the film shines in its action sequences, featuring well-executed hand-to-hand combat scenes.
reviews.author: Tatat Bunnag

reviews.text: The Killer is intriguing due to Michael Fassbender in the lead role and David Fincher's direction, but the script goes nowhere fast.
reviews.author: Jon Mendelsohn

reviews.text: Despite a measured performance from Fassbender and a clear vision/understanding of world-building in Fincher’s approach to visual storytelling, The Killer lacks any kind of teeth.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: David Fincher’s latest thriller, The Killer, is cold to the touch and might even seem impenetrable, but it contains multitudes for anyone interested in finding meaning.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: David Fincher’s Jeanne Dielman.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: Fassbender puts in a straight, steely-eyed performance as he goes through his death list, with director David Fincher giving the straightforward crime drama some strong doses of noir style, especially as the killer gets down to the dirty work.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: A master class in hitmanship given by a deluded teacher...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The Killer is dead on arrival—a cheerless bit of 21st century pop existentialism
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: David Fincher’s latest is a minimalist epic about  a contract killer who appears to have no personality whatsoever. Despite all this, it is a wildly entertaining effort.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: The Killer provides a lurid kind of escapism we haven’t really seen since the ’60s, a suave, cold-blooded but very, very funny kind of savoir-faire.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: This revenge odyssey is minor Fincher, but executed nonetheless in style.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: Fincher re-teams with Andrew Kevin Walker to such seamless ends that it feels like two or three years have passed since their last collaboration instead of nearly 30.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: THE KILLER is a return to form for David Fincher.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Craftsmanship doesn’t quite raise The Killer to the level of art, but in a sea of streaming options, it creates an island of pleasure, however fleeting.
reviews.author: Nate Bell

reviews.text: Michael Fassbender's modern hitman murders people from an abandoned WeWork, eats tactical McMuffins , and sounds like AJ Soprano. Wonderful.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: David Fincher's The Killer is an intriguing character study in and of itself, with no gimmicks, that has enough layers to emerge as one of the best works the iconic filmmaker has delivered in the past ten years.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: The Killer is pure David Fincher – moody, atmospheric, gloomy, and suffused with a thread of dark, sardonic humor.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Within the first five seconds, The Killer gives off major Cool Girl energy as David Fincher’s sleekest film It is a true, technical treat for longtime Fincher Fans, proving why he is a master of the digital film age.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: The Killer is what happens when you take [an action thriller]... and put it in the hands of master craftspersons and artists who elevate every aspect of the production, so that the whole becomes ever greater than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Mark Hughes

reviews.text: In addition to being a smart movie, the action here is also good. As far as movies that get you inside the head of a killer, this is up there.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Here’s the thing… you will know in the first 10 minutes whether you are into this film or hate it and never want to be in this man’s head every again. It’s not a “maybe it will change” kind of situation. In or out.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: This story of a lone contract killer is shallow, familiar, and based on pessimistic and narrow philosophies of life, but it's rich with craft and style. The Killer moves beautifully and is never boring.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: For all the sleek and stylish espionage and action that Fincher delivers with this film, it’s also arguably his funniest.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Under a different filmmaker, The Killer would be your standard assassin flick with overblown action scenes and idiotic side characters. Fincher makes The Killer distinctly his, a lean and methodical look at the job itself...
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Washed-out and callowly nihilistic as a narrative but tasty cinema.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Fincher is adept at excoriating the darkness of the human soul, but he's missed his mark with a character so blindly determined to prove he doesn't have one.
reviews.author: Maureen Lee Lenker

reviews.text: The Killer is an engrossing ride along with a hired gun, made by an artist who never wastes his canvas.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: ... There is something in the coldness that defines The Killer that prevents it from shining as brightly as [Fincher's] other titles. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Though The Killer isn't by far the best from [Fincher], it's beyond entertaining and enjoyable... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The film is a veritable tone poem on the nature of work in the modern world. The Killer is a simultaneously hollow and profound meditation on the numerous ways identity has been swallowed up and voided by the various demands of commerce and brand.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: I loved this film and enjoyed the inner monologue from this concise killer, Fassbender delivers a deadly wink and a nod. I give it an A grade.
reviews.author: Derek Sante

reviews.text: The 70s-influenced thriller moves at a steady pace venturing into neo-noir territory. The visual palette is crisp and sharp with plenty of Fassbender closeups and a downtempo score by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross that prowls through each frame.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Michael Fassbender is fantastic in this role... This is very stylized film from David Fincher and it's really well-done.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: Even when having fun in a violent world of contract killing, Fincher sprinkles in a taste of his worldview. It’s a poignant statement on who holds power.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: When it comes to themes of power, control, and attention to detail, this might be the closest thing David Fincher has come to giving us a “personal” film.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: David Fincher’s ice-cold kind of comedy is admirable, and a good exercise for the analytical. But what I couldn’t figure out is why all of this didn’t add up to something more fun.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Controlled by a tracked heartbeat and activated by a neck crack, watching this man make preparations and blankness fiery with potential energy is utterly captivating.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: The Killer’s observations and commentary are very similar to The Watchmen’s Rorschach. Unfortunately, we’re trapped watching this dull hitman’s actions.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: …annoyingly familiar tale of an assassin’s creed, full of sound and fury, but signifying absolutely nothing…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The Killer is ultimately Minor Fincher, which of course is better than Major Lots of Other People.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: ... draws us in through a wry and sardonic sense of humor, and resists transitioning into a conventional morality tale. It’s simply a good film about a bad man.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Fincher’s craft is on display here as you may not find yourself on the edge of your seat, but your mind will be constantly engaged. This is one of those movies that won’t need you to power through the slowness...
reviews.author: Dhaval Roy

reviews.text: t moves and weaves through its story and the mind of the assassin in a way that doesn’t give the viewers a chance to realize they’re rooting for a murderer-for-hire, and that’s exhilarating.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The Killer has an old-fashioned feel and still manages to nail its target by bringing dashes of freshness, wit and unpredictability to this well-worn genre.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: For fans of the director’s distinctive style, The Killer may be worth a watch, but it may leave some viewers craving a deeper and more emotionally resonant story.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: The Killer is an excellent thriller put together by a master in the genre. While there aren’t any surprises in the plot, this is a visually stunning yet uncomfortable-to-watch movie elevated by its star-studded cast.
reviews.author: Lori Meek

reviews.text: What exists on the page reads as isolated, yet Fincher and Fassbender play it as internal, even intimate.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: The rest of The Killer – its seamless visual aesthetic, the dread-filled score, the episodic rhythm – echoes this oddly meta coming-of-age arc...
reviews.author: Rahul Desai

reviews.text: Besides possessing a notable presence, Michael Fassbender is gifted with magnetism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: The Killer’s target dodged a bullet. Viewers who skip this film can, too.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: [A] slick, brutal and utterly brilliant action movie.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: The Killer is a comical character assassination.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: This cold and calculated assassin is played effortlessly by Michael Fassbender. There is a calming intensity throughout and an excellent score to elevate each moment. The film isn’t always as thrilling as it wants to be, but it sticks with you.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Leave it to Fincher to find something personal in an ode to impersonality.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: It's Fincher's deliciously depraved conceit that his perfectionist process is not unlike the killer's. In his hands, and a mesmerizing title turn from Fassbinder, what could have been a hitman cliche becomes a tangle of loose ends hauntingly left untied.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The Killer a pointless film about the pointlessness of existence. But, like, Fincher.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: [T]echnical proficiency and stylish visuals and to a certain extent, [Michael] Fassbender’s perfectly-typecast nameless killer role aren’t enough to overcome the movie’s overall dull and uninvolving story.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: The film is a lean, often brutal globe-trotting adventure with a solid performance by Fassbender and stand-out sound design.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: Everything is in its right place and the result is a stylish and slick revenge thriller, but you will be wishing there was a bit more to it.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: It’s like “Fight Club” and “The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo” came together to create the most Fincher-y movie ever. This film is a mood, and that mood screams David Fincher.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The two hours patiently go by in a steady telling of revenge as Fassbender methodically stalks his prey and eliminates those who wronged him. Even though some moments are exciting, the overall narrative is similar to wallpaper, it just exists as we watch.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: Everything here is tantalizingly close to calculated perfection that it comes almost as a surprise how The Killer ends up missing its mark.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: This outing bears his indelible mark of quality, even if, in the director’s prodigious filmography, “The Killer” amounts to minor Fincher.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: I'm not suggesting his story cries out for a sequel, but by the time this very dark comedy reaches its strangely sunny ending, you're curious to see what job this killer — and Fincher himself — might take on next.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: The Killer is not Fincher’s best; it’s more of an offbeat character study with impressive production values than a fully realized drama.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The character is boring and so is this movie, but like the supremely skilled Fincher, who can’t help but make images that hold your gaze even as your mind wanders, Fassbender does keep you watching.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: You’ll eat it up and watch it again, perhaps only to realize that maybe there’s something deeper that’s being said about a general lack of empathy in a short-sighted world where we often feel we just need to get the job done, no matter the toll.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: It is that attention to detail that makes The Killer a precise and meticulous thriller, displaying the various reasons why David Fincher does not miss.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: 'The Killer' is grimly entertaining and although it may not be a laugh-a-minute comedy or a wham-bam-actioner, it still has more than ample style and substance to make it worth the time.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Though the film's neo-noir nature allows Fincher to indulge in some sinfully entertaining displays of violence, much of its actual power lies in using the protagonist's chosen vocation as an entry point into commentary on the nature of the gig economy.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: While The Killer represents something of a stylistic endpoint for Fincher, however, it does demonstrate the limits of simply following things out to their logical conclusion, in that one is left wondering whether more could have been done.
reviews.author: Lawrence Garcia

reviews.text: David Fincher sticks to the "plan," albeit sometimes to a fault. Still, if that's the film's only real miss, then like its titular character, The Killer is definitely one to watch out for.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: The Killer's globe-trotting plot is self-explanatory and is not remotely close to being a top-tier David Fincher film.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The Killer is an incredibly nuanced and introspective feature that would be among the cream of any other film catalogue....Fincher proves himself to be one of the most exciting, observant, and oddly human filmmakers working today.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: If you are expecting a solid, well-crafted character piece you'll be satisfied
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: ...one of the best and most spellbinding thrillers to come out of Hollywood in a good long while.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The director’s stylistic touch and smooth visionary aesthetic can’t outweigh the pretentious undertone and egregious narration accompanying the director’s intuition.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: While it doesn’t have the thematic depth or resonance to quite matchup to Fincher’s masterpieces Se7en, The Social Network and Zodiac, The Killer is undoubtedly a slowly engrossing and subversive take on the assassin film.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: Fincher trusts the faces of his actors... His faith in Fassbender is amply rewarded -- even the way the actor’s arms smoothly swing past his hips is expressive -- but Fincher is the true star of the film.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: When it comes to breathlessness, it's no Bourne, but the antihero allure of the bucket hat-wearing, Smiths-loving contractor gives Fassbender a perfect comeback role.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: 'The Killer' might be described as anti-philosophical, at least in the sense that The Killer is constantly undercutting his own self-important mental blather.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: [W]e are treated to a cavalcade of slick assassinations strung together by the barest minimum of a plot. All the better to savor Michael Fassbender at his most ominous, reminding us at varying points in his narration that empathy is a weakness.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Like watching a magnificent athlete on a Stairmaster.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Stylish and occasionally amusing, but it’s essentially a one-joke affair that Fincher and Fassbender are unable to sustain.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Moments of extraordinary brutality are to be found here, but its greatest success is in its quiet self-assurance.
reviews.author: Keri O'Shea

reviews.text: At heart, an elevator pitch for a two-hour pilot for a slick, junky Netflix series about a globe-trotting assassin.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: It’s a great match between director and subject, and emerges as one of the best films of its kind you’ll see this year.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: Prime David Fincher, a cleverly-crafted revenge thriller that keeps you on your toes.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: As slight and as inconsequential as it may be, the film is still quite amusing, even if it does vanish from memory not too long after the story’s events have concluded.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: A cold and calculated study not of a profession but of the practice of discipline.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: The Killer is just, well, good. A good, straightforward film.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: The Killer feels like a style exercise more than anything else, and it’s a successful one. That may make the film seem slight... But don’t let that fool you. Just like the films that inspired it, there’s much more going on beneath the surface.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: The Killer is a lean, sparse and surprisingly funny entry into the betrayed-assassin school of film-making, based on a French graphic novel series of the same name.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: It’s not Fincher’s best film by any stretch, not with a resume that includes “Zodiac,” “The Social Network” and “Fight Club.” But it’s an intriguing one.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Fincher makes hay with his main character’s worst fears, and the result is a hard, nasty, droll, bullet-fast piece of film-making... that hijacks your nervous system for two hours before releasing you, pleasantly exhausted, into the cool night air.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: For David Fincher, the opportunity to craft a story around another obsessed individual with a flexible sense of morality makes plenty of sense. Fortunately, he lined up his shot and executed it brilliantly.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: The film is in thrall to the movie mythology of the assassin and to the slick cynicism of Fincher’s own back catalogue.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: It’s nice to see the genius filmmaker dipping back into genre, so to speak, with a clean and clinical thriller.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: It’s not fair, of course, to stack up every film against the full canon of its maker. But there certainly doesn't feel much of substance here -- no level of thematic or narrative differentiation that would stake a grander claim to its reason for being.
reviews.author: Brent Simon

reviews.text: Pure provocative tension. Nothing but stress-producing filmmaking. Fincher’s masterful triumphant is one of the year’s best films. No sign of pink, philosophical regrets, mean white men or a conflicted sex life.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: Michael Fassbender and Tilda Swinton give this narration-heavy thriller a few big kicks. (mini-review)
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: It’s evil lurking within the ordinary and fueled by technological paranoia. The act of killing isn’t the main event; it’s the mundane procedures that come before it
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: The cast is great, the concept is interesting, but there’s something in the execution that leaves the wallop the narrative seems to strive for to fall flat.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: It may be a tale built around vengeance, but there’s an existentialism to the film’s look at death that is gorgeously precise and darkly comedic.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: A dark and slick thriller featuring a protagonist of, let’s just say, highly questionable morals. Welcome back, David Fincher.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: David Fincher directs another thrilling sensory experience...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: A film that is almost as objective as the killer himself, and just as intelligent.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: This isn’t an unpleasant movie. This is an unfeeling movie.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Even though The Killer is coming out during the time of year when prestige movies usually come out, and it’s played a couple of film festivals, it’s not really that kind of movie, and I say that as a compliment.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: It’s not as good as Se7en, Fight Club, Mank or other Fincher films such as The Curious Case of Benjamin Button (2008), The Social Network (2010) and Gone Girl (2014), but fans will appreciate this humorous walk on the noir side.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: A low-key slow burn that examines the moral relativism we all excuse in our lives.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: The Killer isn't the best work from the stars and filmmakers of this somewhat predictable drama about an assassin who goes on a personal vendetta. However, the movie's performances are above-average. The voiceover narration will get mixed reactions.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The Killer works well as a macabre thriller, as satire of the corporate (tech) world and one’s precarious position within it.
reviews.author: Ana Yorke

reviews.text: The Killer may not be Fincher's best work but, within its narrow constraints, it nails its moves.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: The thriller genre is where Fincher belongs, and The Killer is our welcome reminder.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: Keoghan is the one who holds this film together by force of presence: his stillness as an actor is remarkable but late on, when huge physical demands are placed on his performance, he responds to the challenge brilliantly.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Much like Drive, it straddles the boundary between making its protagonist iconic and a subject of parody, the paucity of their inner lives at war with their attractive ability to escape tangled webs and be active forces of nature.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Passing through Florida in one scene, our murderous protagonist says, "Where else can you find so many like-minded individuals outside a penitentiary?"
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: There's nothing I hate more than going to a car rental dealership, and even that looks cool in this movie.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Fincher's continued fascination with the darker side of society makes for compelling viewing, and getting another great Fassbender performance is icing on the cake.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Again, and this cannot be understated, the movie has no purpose. It is the umpteen millionth pensive hitman movie. It is the eleventy billionth brooding urban crime thriller. It is the thousandy gazillionth revenge opus.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: It occurs to me that this film, adapted from a French graphic novel and which reunites Fincher with his “Se7en” screenwriter Andrew Kevin Walker, is the closest thing to comedy that the director will ever do.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: From a filmmaker who tends to scrub the fingerprints off his own work, this is a brilliant take on how we are all disconnected and fading into anonymity doing soulless and impersonal jobs in the era of WeWork, Amazon, UberEats and streaming services.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Brilliant filmmaking without a heartbeat. The eponymous killer is a big nobody.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: The film is a richly crafted fresh spin on a well-traveled genre that’s every bit as meticulous and calculated as its titular lead character.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A very entertaining movie and bears a lot of Fincher’s hallmarks, but ultimately a bit forgettable
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: It’s a movie that never raises its voice, forcing you to lean in and listen carefully lest you miss a single word.
reviews.author: Michael Nordine

reviews.text: The Killer is a visually striking and philosophically engaging thriller that never amounts to anything particularly special, and asks whether that’s such a bad thing.
reviews.author: Kyle Logan

reviews.text: The Killer is a slickly made, stylish thriller, with an anxiety inducing score from Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross, that uses the central character’s aloofness as a hook to pull you to the edge of your seat.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Mr. Fassbender combines the inhuman calculations of his android from “Prometheus” with the misogynistic hatred of his contract killer from “Haywire” into a joyless performance that’s impossible to care about.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: The Killer is cold, calculated, perfection! An Instantly became one of my favorites from David Fincher!
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: “The Killer” is a slick and amoral thriller that’s as stone-cold as its protagonist.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Fassbender, marking a welcome return after a four-year time-out, of course, is key. A remarkable presence, he’s able to grip our attention, often single-handedly.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: More of an aesthetic exercise than anything else. Impeccably assembled.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The pretentious and the silly may consider themselves opposites, but frequently they are close companions. They certainly are in Andrew Kevin Walker’s screenplay.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: The Killer is as cold and laconic as his antihero, trapped, for better or worse in its intransigence and perfectionism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: Fincher is on his home turf here, and he works with the confidence of a director who is making his 12th movie and taking one for himself. He hits a clean bullseye.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Whatever way you watch “The Killer” – at the theater or streaming at home – you will see a tightly made, always interesting story of an assassin who finally wants out – on his terms.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: ... With The Killer, Fincher recuperates the best of his craftsmanship, even when it is an adaptation and tempting to lump it in the same bag of previous examples that share the same idea. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillermo Courau

reviews.text: A slick neo-noir thriller, seamlessly executed by master filmmaker David Fincher. A sharp and stylish character study that's simple in approach and story, yet heavy on the killer's method, focus and psyche. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Fans of Seven, Fight Club, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Zodiac will be happy enough but The Killer lacks originality or any hint of human warmth and it’s unlikely to win him the Oscar he’s been denied so far.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: Though The Killer is not a character who invites sympathy for his plight, he does somehow elicit our support for his quest.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Even still, Fincher fans will find plenty to love about “The Killer,” as it plays like his greatest hits while taking us on a zippy and entertaining ride.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Dazzlingly precise entertainment, and not as simple as it seems. [Full review in Spanush]
reviews.author: Nando Salvá

reviews.text: And the real affront is that The Killer isn’t even a terrible movie. It is worse than that. It is endlessly, grindingly competent.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Fincher takes what could be an impersonal story and turns it into the most self-reflective film in his career, and those who appreciate his particular auteuristic tendencies—from obsession to process, both on and offscreen—will savor the result.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: I wasn’t expecting a black comedy, but that is just what director David Fincher has given us with his procedural reverse character study of a man whose strong ideas about his own identity prove somewhat unfounded.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: While it's nice to see Fincher getting back to basics, focusing an entire movie on a character who aims to be as forgettable as possible seems to serve as a metaphor for most Netflix originals.
reviews.author: Patrick Cavanaugh

reviews.text: It's really a character study of a working-class stiff, of the kind that Raymond Carver would enjoy.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: By applying our technocapitalist present to the kind of person that this reality inevitably creates, Fincher’s created a thoroughly entertaining look at a pathetic crook—all while delivering a self-deprecating blow to clockwork living.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: Routine material made all the more engrossing thanks to some cinematic manipulation.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Neither the film nor the character is particularly special, but they are good enough at what they set out to do.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: “The Killer” may look like a fight for one’s life with a satisfying side of vengeance. But it’s a study of an existential death served in delectably cold and precise portions.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: It’s arguably the greatest expression yet of Fincher’s style and worldview—caustic, unrelenting, and wickedly funny.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: This is a very simple and straightforward noir thriller story you’ve seen before but its a well polished with Fincher’s  meticulous approach. This is a pretty high quality thriller but lacks the depth and complexity of Fincher’s best work.
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: The Killer is Fincher at his funniest delivering a violent satire that few people could possibly misread.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: The Killer is mesmerising in its own way. It imprisons you in the mind of an amoral assassin and lulls you into believing the ethics of murder is neither here nor there, all that matters is effectiveness.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: A suffocating, acerbic plunge into noir-ish action and reaction, offering actor Michael Fassbender one of his best roles in one of Fincher’s best pictures.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: This is a series of nastily entertaining, stylishly crafted revenge murders that accomplishes its goal of exploring the mind of a contract killer, nothing more, nothing less
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Fassbender is at once blankly reptilian while also wearing the weight of his character’s ceaseless calculations and manoeuvres. To be both a chilling screen presence yet one we can’t help but cheer for is quite something.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: This is a blast and it does what it does so well.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: It’s cool, scuzzy, and imbued with healthy doses of thoughtfulness and coal black humour.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: With a plot as predictable as it is simple, it must be said that Fincher has the necessary arsenal so that we can pleasantly spend two hours watching The Killer knowing everything that will happen from minute 5. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernando E. Juan Lima

reviews.text: At times intoxicating to the point of addiction; others, too cold and precious, The Killer has certain irruptions of ironic humor that make it too self-aware, but... the director's shots rescue the script from its own clichés. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: David Fincher delivers a meticulously executed thriller about an assassin with a target on his own back who launches on a complex revenge scheme. Not an entirely new idea but still terrific.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: This is a lesser work from the filmmaker, but even his lesser entries are better than most of what we get these days. Sometimes it's okay to let an artist play the hits.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: “The Killer” is eminently watchable, especially when Tilda Swinton shows up.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A finely tooled exercise in dirty work, this is a lean, mean descent into a deadly “professional” underworld with dozens of ways to die——especially if you cross paths with The Killer.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Another meticulous masterpiece of Fincher filmmaking, with Fassbender's stone cold nihilist providing a solid foundation for a compelling and brilliantly realised film.
reviews.author: Lisa Giles-Keddie

reviews.text: Really solid. 100% Fincher. Fassbender is perfectly cast for the meticulous nature of the character. It moves fast, with some great action. Honestly I just loved how the film broke down the logistics of being an assassin. Not a guy you want to piss off.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: This is David Fincher’s version of a sitcom: as violently funny as it is hilariously violent.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The film isn’t out to subvert the genre, exactly, but it does understand the genre.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The Killer is a gripping, stone-cold thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. Fincher masterfully takes us into the psyche of a contract killer, a dark and haunting place that paradoxically exudes a sinister allure.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: Although The Killer is a crisply told piece of pulpy neo-noir, it also has an element of self-parody to it, laying out a consummate professional’s precise process and then dashing it into chaos at every chance.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: The antithesis to the latest string of hitmen movies: a meditative paced film that replaces booming bass & gunfire for an ASMR Michael Fassbender voiceover.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: It looks terrific, churning skilfully through action, intrigue and pitch-black drama, each scene infused with wry wit and icy violence. Yet while the artistry is first-rate, the film lacks an emotional connection that might have pulled us in deeper.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: No matter how many hitman sagas have gone before, you owe it to yourself to see director David Fincher’s take on such material with his new film. Quite simply, it slays.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: THE KILLER is a CALCULATED, SINISTER and THRILLING return to form for David Fincher. Fassbender's icy charisma & flawless sound design create a RAZOR-SHARP experience that lingers. Trent Reznor & Atticus Ross elevate tension with their haunting score.
reviews.author: Shahbaz Siddiqui

reviews.text: A wildly entertaining, thrilling and wickedly funny ride.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: David Fincher brings his thrilling auteur vision to an actioner bursting at the seams with existential philosophy. A deeply introspective protagonist explains the nuances of his murderous methodology. The Killer will have you glued to the screen.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: It turns out that great filmmakers sometimes can’t elevate ho-hum material, and can sometimes even hinder it.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Fincher’s shark-like forward motion glides right through... Themes of masculinity and flickering humanity can’t, though, elevate his most glib, inconsequential film, which wastes the still luckless Fassbender, too.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: "The Killer" may be based on a graphic novel by Alexis “Matz” Nolent, but it feels like Fincher's most personal film to date.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: It’s a perfect match of director to material, with a phalanx of great artists at the height of their powers aiding him in that mission.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Michael Fassbender and David Fincher make quite the pair. A dark, twisted, and thrilling noir that will have viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. Fassbender is captivating.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: [A] deliciously twisty thriller... the longer you stare unblinking at The Killer, the harder it stares back. And the more the emptiness underneath its eyes starts to feel like a feature, not a bug. A steely dissection of sociopathy.
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: A riveting revenge riot, with gobsmacking levels of film craft, and a performance from Michael Fassbender to make your blood run cold. It’s not quite top-tier Fincher, but it comes damn close.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: The Killer is an action film with verve and brains to spare.
reviews.author: Perry Norton

reviews.text: There are some slight indications of discretion, expertly defined to Fassbender’s physicality – but he’s a man on a murderous clean-up mission, and nothing will deter him from completing the mission.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: The Killer is a savage and savagely funny thriller from David Fincher.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: The Killer is an icy-cold thriller encircling an assassin’s philosophical crisis with a mesmerizing performance from Fassbender.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: It’s cold to the touch and clearly won’t be for everyone, but The Killer finds Fincher back to his Vantablack best with a lean, meticulous, and intermittently cruel exercise in top-tier filmmaking.
reviews.author: Matt Rodgers

reviews.text: David Fincher dabbles in the pleasures of genre without ever allowing the tlandish scenario to be treated with more respect than it deserves.
reviews.author: David Robb

reviews.text: Fincher and Fassbender are a match made in crime-noir heaven, and I hope they find another project to work together on soon.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: My instinct is that appreciation for The Killer will grow with time, as we get used the muted emotional tenor we didn't expect from a Fincher movie.
reviews.author: Alexander Harrison

reviews.text: If The Killer teaches us anything, it’s that any director, no matter how legendary they are, can fall victim to a bad script. While Fincher’s iconic style permeates the two-hour runtime, the hollow plot and uninspired writing are impossible to ignore.
reviews.author: Emma Kiely

reviews.text: Fincher’s movie struggles to find its modus operandi.
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: The Killer never stops being fun... but always while watching the clock to see when the movie will end. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: A gripping, if somewhat formulaic hit man thriller, with a decidedly unexpected soundtrack of Smiths songs.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: It's moody, stylish, and pretty preposterous, but thoroughly watchable...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Even if this is a story we've seen many times before, it's still a damn fine assassin film.
reviews.author: Alex Billington

reviews.text: It's incredibly frustrating to watch it meander around numerous bends, finding only the tiniest handful of exciting or bleakly funny scenes.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Fincher deserved it all [appaluse] and then some for The Killer's dark, noir-ish, eminently watchable kill-fest.
reviews.author: Jack King

reviews.text: The Killer ends up seeming hollow and pointless.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Fincher creates one of his most precise and rigorous works, although his samurai-filmmaker gaze also trembles when romance pokes its head through the story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: [David Fincher] rebuilds the revenge genre with the fervor and precision of a time bomb, one second away from going boom! [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: Fassbender is well cast and gives a typically committed performance... However. The Killer also often drifts into the realm of self-conscious pastiche. It’s questionable, too, whether Fincher brings anything fresh to the genre.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: At the risk of getting all Robert McKee on you, the voiceover gets grating fast, and is not as clever or amusing as Fincher and his screenwriter Andrew Kevin Walker thinks it is. A little less conversation, a little more action, please.
reviews.author: Marlow Stern

reviews.text: Marrying a tight and effective script from Andrew Kevin Walker, smart performances from Michael Fassbender and Tilda Swinton, and sharp editing, this assassin odyssey is one you’ll want to watch again and again.
reviews.author: Lex Briscuso

reviews.text: Fassbender looks lean and mean, but for all his monologuing he has the depth of a non-player character. There’s nothing wrong with it. It’s a mission gone right. It certainly has its moments, but The Killer feels like a Netflix film through and through.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: Like a hollow-point shell, David Fincher’s slickly enjoyable assassin thriller is explosive but empty.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Straightforward and enjoyable, it’s a slickly paced, country hopping glossy exercise about an emotionless man who has to annihilate some goons before he gets got, nothing more.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Rather, there is something ever so gently unhinged in this lean, crisp action film that doubles as an arthouse character study; something just a little askew in its perspective, giving it an inviting absurdity.
reviews.author: Caspar Salmon

reviews.text: The Killer allows [Fincher] to exercise his own perfectionist instincts in a raw entertainment that makes a virtue of its emotional distance. It may prove to be Fincher’s first self-help film.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: There’s a hint of the self-righteous “incel” about him (see the Smiths fetish), which is what makes the movie interesting.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It’s a lurid crime thriller that, to some degree, chimes with Fincher’s 1995 masterpiece Se7en.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: as well as describing the Killer’s line of work, the idea of “enduring boredom” also applies to our experience of watching the movie — but that is entirely the point of the film.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: With The Killer, David Fincher returns to form with a film that plays to his directorial strengths and artistry.
reviews.author: Rory O'Connor

reviews.text: A competently realized crime thriller made by a technical team just as sharply attuned to details as the director at the ship’s helm, the Netflix production is entertaining but a little orthodox.
reviews.author: Rafaela Sales Ross

reviews.text: "execution is everything"... The Killer is a well executed thriller however like the titular protagonist’s handiwork, it is not quite the perfect hit.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: It’s as unfeeling as any Fincher thriller, at once predictable in its simplicity but also strangely daring because of it.
reviews.author: Ryan Lattanzio

reviews.text: The film executes its purpose with a liquid carbon dioxide-billowing icy resolve.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: ... It’s pretty bog standard stuff, albeit directed and acted very deftly.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: Fincher in fun mode and Fassbender ahem, killing it. Hits the mark.
reviews.author: Jane Crowther

reviews.text: This being a David Fincher joint, the answers aren’t pretty, while the images are nearly always sublime.
reviews.author: Ben Croll

reviews.text: A few moments in the film do get the blood up, but otherwise The Killer is curiously inert, its wheels spinning with little traction.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: It's not exactly an ambitious plotline for someone like Fincher, but it's certainly an engaging one, and the cryptic, constantly evasive protagonist is a puzzle that lingers after the credits roll.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Fincher seems to be having a great deal of fun with The Killer.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: For the most part, this slays.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: There’s a thin line between self-reflection and self-parody, and The Killer comes dangerously close to crossing it a few too many times.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: It’s not that he’s anything less than great at it, but [Fincher] may think there’s more shading, more revelation in how he has staged “The Killer” than there actually is.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: This is a thriller of pure surface and style and managed with terrific flair and Fassbender’s careworn, inscrutable face is just right for it.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: For all the inherent familiarity of the hit-man genre, Fincher and Walker have nonetheless crafted an absorbing tale; what it has to offer that’s any different from countless similar tales lies in the minutiae rather than the mayhem.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: The Killer is unquestionably the simplest, most straightforward movie of David Fincher's career, for better and for worse. A case of admiration more than enjoyment.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: This may not demonstrate the absolute heights that Fincher can achieve. Still, it is a welcomed reminder that when it comes to gritty investigations of violent circumstances, few people can do it better.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text: The Killer is almost a B-movie, committing to the trappings of its genre and embracing schlockiness like previous Fincher films Panic Room and The Game. Nothing wrong with that.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

synopsis: After a fateful near-miss an assassin battles his employers, and himself, on an international manhunt he insists isn't personal.
